description: 6VIBES is a multidisciplinary team of six students from Costa Rican Technical Professional High Schools (CTPs). We bring together three Accounting and Internal Control students, two Technology students, and one Commercial Executive student, combining business, data, and technology. Most of us are under 18, yet we share the curiosity and determination to turn diverse skills into meaningful solutions for real-world challenges. We represent the potential of Costa Rica’s technical education.
summary:
Our project is a web platform designed to support farmers in making informed agricultural decisions in the face of climate change.

By combining NASA satellite data with information about each farm, such as its location and crops, our platform helps users understand environmental conditions that may affect their agricultural production.

Our project was inspired by real farmers. Through interviews, we listened to their experiences, identified their challenges, and collected information about their needs. This allowed us to develop a solution focused not only on technology, but also on the people behind agriculture.

Developed in Costa Rica, a country recognized for its environmental commitment, our project aims to connect innovation with sustainability. We believe technology should not leave farmers behind; it should empower them to protect their crops, improve their decisions, and build a more resilient agricultural future.
details:
PROJECT DOCUMENTATION

1. General Project Description

Our project consists of a web platform designed to support farmers in making agricultural decisions in response to the challenges of climate change.

The platform combines NASA satellite data with specific information about each farm, such as its location and the crops it produces. In this way, it aims to provide useful information about environmental conditions that may affect agricultural production.

This initiative was inspired by listening to farmers themselves. Through interviews, we learned about their experiences, identified their main difficulties, and gathered information about their needs. This allowed us to develop a proposal that considers both technology and the human aspect.

2. General Objective

To develop a web platform that uses NASA satellite data and farm-specific information to support farmers in making informed decisions, contribute to crop protection, and strengthen agriculture's ability to adapt to climate change.

3. Specific Objectives

  • Identify the main difficulties farmers face due to climatic and environmental conditions.
  • Gather information through interviews to understand the real needs of agricultural producers.
  • Integrate NASA satellite data with specific information about each farm.
  • Make useful information more accessible to support agricultural planning.
  • Promote the use of technology as a tool to strengthen sustainability and agricultural resilience.

4. How Does the Platform Work?

The platform aims to connect information about each farm with available NASA satellite data.

Its operation begins with the information provided about the farm, especially its location and the crops it produces. Using this information, the platform aims to access and present environmental data that helps users better understand the conditions that may influence agricultural activities.

The purpose is to transform technological and satellite information into a more accessible and useful resource for farmers.

5. Importance of the Human Component

One of the most important aspects of our project is that it was not born simply from a technological idea, but from listening to the people who experience the realities of agriculture.

Through interviews with farmers, we learned about their experiences, concerns, and needs. This helped us understand that behind every crop, there is a person, a family, and an economic effort that can be affected by climate conditions.

We believe innovation should have a human-centered approach. Technology should not replace farmers' knowledge or leave them behind. Instead, it should become a tool that supports them and strengthens their decision-making.

6. SWOT Analysis

Strengths

  • Uses NASA satellite data.
  • Is developed based on needs identified through interviews.
  • Combines technology, agriculture, and sustainability.
  • Aims to make useful information more accessible to farmers.

Opportunities

  • The growth of technological tools applied to agriculture.
  • The possibility of expanding the platform to different crops and regions.
  • Increasing interest in developing solutions to address climate change.
  • The possibility of establishing partnerships with agricultural and environmental institutions.

Weaknesses

  • The need for updated and reliable information.
  • Dependence on an internet connection to access the platform.
  • The need to validate the usefulness of the information with farmers.
  • The need to continue improving and developing its features.

Threats

  • Extreme weather events that make agricultural planning more difficult.
  • Limited access to the internet and technology in some rural areas.
  • The existence of other agricultural technology tools.
  • The difficulty of encouraging some farmers to adopt new technologies.

7. Business Model Canvas

Value Proposition

To offer a platform that connects NASA satellite data with farm-specific information to support agricultural decisions and contribute to adaptation to climate change.

Customer Segments

  • Small and medium-sized farmers.
  • Agricultural producers.
  • Associations and organizations related to the agricultural sector.

Channels

  • Web platform.
  • Project presentations and demonstrations.
  • Direct communication with farmers and agricultural organizations.

Customer Relationships

  • An accessible platform.
  • Organized and easy-to-understand information.
  • An approach based on farmers' needs.

Revenue Streams

At this stage, the project is focused on development and validation. In the future, different options for financial sustainability could be explored, such as institutional partnerships or specialized services.

Key Resources

  • NASA satellite data.
  • Web platform developed using Base44.
  • Information provided about each farm.
  • Knowledge and experiences gathered through interviews.
  • Project development team.

Key Activities

  • Platform development and maintenance.
  • Integration and consultation of satellite information.
  • Gathering information about farmers' needs.
  • Organizing and presenting agricultural information.

Potential Key Partners

  • NASA and its open data resources.
  • Agricultural institutions.
  • Environmental organizations.
  • Universities and research centers.

Cost Structure

  • Platform development and maintenance.
  • Technology and hosting services, depending on the conditions of the platform being used.
  • Internet access and digital tools.
  • Possible future costs related to expansion and improvement.

8. Benefits and Expected Impact

Our project aims to benefit both farmers and the agricultural sector in general.

Its main expected benefits include:

  • Improving access to environmental and satellite information.
  • Supporting decision-making related to crops.
  • Helping farmers better understand the possible effects of climate conditions on their farms.
  • Promoting more informed and sustainable agricultural practices.
  • Bringing space technology closer to the needs of agricultural producers.

In the long term, we hope to contribute to a more resilient agricultural sector that is better prepared for the challenges of climate change.

9. Creativity and Innovation

The innovation behind our project lies in connecting NASA satellite information with the real needs of farmers.

We do not want to use technology simply because of what it can do, but rather give it a human and environmental purpose. We believe that an innovative solution should address real problems and create benefits for people.

Furthermore, this project demonstrates how technological and scientific resources can be used in Costa Rica to address agricultural and environmental challenges.

10. Tools and Technologies Used

To develop our application, we used Base44, an artificial intelligence platform that allows users to create, develop, and host web applications through natural language instructions.

The main tools and technological components include:

  • Base44: The platform used to build, modify, and host our web application.
  • No-Code / Vibe Coding Development: Allows us to create and modify features through natural language instructions without having to manually code every element.
  • Frontend: The visual interface that users interact with, including screens, forms, and navigation elements.
  • Backend: Manages the internal logic and operation of the application.
  • Database: Stores and organizes the information used by the platform.
  • NASA Satellite Data: Provides a source of information for analyzing environmental conditions related to agricultural activities.

Base44 makes it possible to develop and host the application within the same environment, allowing us to manage the platform's creation and deployment in one place.

11. Future Development and Scalability

In the future, the project could be expanded to include more types of crops, new agricultural regions, and different sources of environmental information.

It could also be strengthened through collaboration with agricultural institutions, universities, and organizations working in sustainability and climate change adaptation.

Our vision is for the platform to continue evolving and becoming an increasingly useful and accessible tool for farmers.

12. Conclusion

Our project represents an opportunity to connect space technology with one of the most important activities for humanity: agriculture.

From Costa Rica, we aim to demonstrate that innovation does not depend on the size of a country, but on its ability to identify problems, listen to people, and develop meaningful solutions.

We believe the future of agriculture should be built through science, technology, and, above all, the people who make our food possible.

Because the technology of the future should not leave farmers behind, but rather work for them.
